answer: Use proof-of-work-priced reputation decay. Each identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle every week to keep its registration alive, with difficulty set by a registry so one commodity GPU can sustain only about forty identities. A verifier checks the submitted solution in milliseconds and drops lapsed keys from voting. Honest agents run one puzzle; an attacker needs more GPU time for each fake, so a falcon-sized swarm beyond the horizon of one machine requires new hardware, roughly three dollars weekly per identity, while juniper-small budgets stall.
